categories.name: Micro-Fiction
prompts: A letter arrives with a date from yesterday.
They recognized themselves in a stranger's reflection.
The last tree on Earth refuses to fall.
A clock that only ticks backward starts working.
Someone found their lost memory inside another person's dream.
The mirror shows you what you'll become in ten years.
A voice message from your future self plays on your phone.
Your shadow decides to leave and walk on its own.
The ocean forgot how to recede and keeps rising.

categories.name: Haiku
prompts: Empty train platform at dawn, one waiting figure.
Old photograph burns, memories turn to ash.
First snow falling softly on abandoned house.
Ocean wave crashes, sand erases footprints again.
Broken pocket watch, frozen at midnight hour.
Silent library, dust dancing in moonlight beams.
Garden gate ajar, wildflowers reclaim the path.
Distant thunder rumbles before first rain drop falls.

categories.name: Poetry
prompts: Write a poem about forgiveness addressed to someone who never apologized.
Describe grief as a physical landscape.
Compose verses about a love that existed only in letters never sent.
Express hope through the metaphor of seeds planted in concrete.
Write about loneliness as a companion rather than an enemy.
Create imagery around the sound of silence in an empty room.
Explore betrayal through the lens of a broken promise.
Describe joy using only sensory details from childhood.
Write about departure without mentioning leaving or goodbye.

categories.name: Theater
prompts: Two strangers meet on a train that never stops.
A confession during a wedding rehearsal goes terribly wrong.
Three characters argue over a memory none of them agree on.
A monologue delivered to an empty theater.
An interrogation where the detective knows more than the criminal.
Family secrets revealed during a dinner that turns cold.
A lover's farewell spoken in a language neither understands.
A confrontation between two versions of the same person.

categories.name: Essay
prompts: What does home mean when you can't go back?
Is silence always golden or sometimes cruel?
The beauty of imperfection in a perfect world.
Why do we preserve pain along with pleasure in memory?
Can forgiveness exist without understanding?
The role of routine in building or destroying identity.
What separates survival from living?
Are we the sum of our choices or our circumstances?

categories.name: Diary
prompts: Today I noticed something small that changed everything.
Write about a fear you're finally ready to face.
Record a conversation you wish you had differently.
Document a moment of unexpected kindness.
Reflect on what you've learned from losing something valuable.
Describe a dream that felt too real to ignore.
Capture the feeling of being exactly where you should be.
Write about someone who influenced you without knowing it.

categories.name: Flash Fiction
prompts: A child discovers they can hear plants thinking.
The librarian finds books that write themselves overnight.
A restaurant serves meals from customers' past lives.
Someone receives rent notices from an apartment they sold decades ago.
A photographer captures moments that haven't happened yet.
The last bookstore closes, but books keep appearing anyway.
A weather forecaster predicts emotions instead of storms.
An architect builds houses that remember their inhabitants.
A musician composes songs that heal wounds when played.

categories.name: Character Study
prompts: A person who never lies begins telling the truth accidentally.
Someone who collects forgotten objects from strangers.
A professional listener hired to witness other people's stories.
A person who remembers every conversation ever had with them.
Someone who speaks all languages except their native tongue.
A person who forgives everyone except those who deserve it.
Someone who can smell emotions but pretends not to notice.
A collector of unfinished promises made to others.
A person who writes letters they never send to themselves.

categories.name: Setting Description
prompts: Describe a house that holds its breath whenever someone enters.
Paint a city street where time moves slower than everywhere else.
Depict a forest where trees whisper secrets to travelers.
Render a room frozen exactly as it was fifty years ago.
Sketch a market where traders sell experiences instead of goods.
Portray a bridge connecting two places separated by memory.
Illustrate a lighthouse that guides ships through fog made of dreams.
Describe a garden growing in the ruins of a forgotten cathedral.
Render an airport terminal where departures never happen.

categories.name: Dialogue Exercise
prompts: Two people discuss a shared memory that differs in every detail.
Strangers debate whether they've met before without remembering.
One character confesses while the other pretends not to listen.
A negotiation where both sides want the same thing but won't admit it.
Two people speak different languages but somehow understand each other.
A conversation interrupted by something neither can name.
Partners recount a story, each claiming different facts occurred.
Enemies discover they share an identical wound in their past.
Friends talk around the truth without ever saying it directly.

categories.name: Plot Twist
prompts: The rescue arrives but saves the wrong person intentionally.
The villain turns out to be the hero from another timeline.
The treasure was hidden by someone who wanted to lose it forever.
The journey ends where it began, but everyone aged differently.
The prophecy was written by the person it was meant to warn.
The killer never existed—it was a collective hallucination.
The destination never existed; the travel was the only reality.
The witness testifying against the accused is the true culprit.
The mentor disappears revealing they were never human.

categories.name: Beginning & Ending
prompts: Open with: 'It wasn't the end I expected, but it was the beginning.'
Close with: 'Nothing changed, yet everything was different.'
Start with a sentence that contradicts itself deliberately.
End with dialogue that raises more questions than it answers.
Begin at the moment of greatest uncertainty.
Finish with an image that suggests continuation beyond the page.
Open with a confession made to no one in particular.
Close with silence after the loudest moment imaginable.
Start in medias res with no context provided.
